extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting systematic reviews in psychology/neuroscience (interoception and dissociation), and other interested scholars/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A preregistered, PRISMA-compliant systematic review protocol examining interoception (accuracy, sensibility, awareness) in relation to dissociation, including baseline comparisons, laboratory-induced state dissociation, and correlational studies. The review targets clinical, symptomatic, and experimentally induced dissociation and compares findings to non-clinical/control conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: The review is preregistered (OSF registration DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/D25PU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and planned methods are specified in advance to reduce bias; registration metadata (date, registry, schema) is provided on OSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The review is described as 'PRISMA-compliant systematic review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review should adhere to PRISMA reporting standards (transparent search strategy, selection flowchart, data extraction and synthesis reporting). The page does not enumerate PRISMA items but invokes overall compliance as a methodological standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition of dissociation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissociation is defined as 'the disruption and disconnection in the usual integration of consciousness, memories, emotions, and sense of self/agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should use an explicit, consistent conceptualization of dissociation so included studies are comparable; this definition frames inclusion and interpretation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit assessment of interoception dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The review will assess interoception and its dimensions (i.e., interoceptive accuracy, sensibility, and awareness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should be categorized and evaluated according to which interoceptive dimension(s) they measure; comparisons and synthesis should respect these distinct constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline vs. post-laboratory induction comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight studies assessing differences in interoception at baseline and following laboratory induction methods to elicit state dissociation compared with a non-clinical or control condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both trait/baseline measures and experimental (state) induction studies; evaluate changes pre/post induction and contrast with controls to assess effects attributable to induced dissociation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of diverse operationalizations of dissociation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include individuals experiencing dissociation as a disorder, as a symptom, or experimentally in the laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility should encompass clinical diagnoses, symptom-level measures, and experimentally induced dissociation so the review captures the full range of operational definitions; subgroup analyses may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to non-clinical/control conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare findings in dissociative conditions to non-clinical or control groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure included studies provide or allow comparison to appropriate control conditions to interpret whether interoceptive differences are specific to dissociation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of correlational evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Review research looking at correlates of interoception and dissociation to capture this relation fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and synthesize correlational studies (associations between interoceptive measures and dissociation measures) in addition to case-control and experimental designs, to provide a comprehensive picture of relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of laboratory induction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess laboratory induction methods used to elicit state dissociation and their effects on interoception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and appraise the types of induction procedures, their validity for producing dissociative states, and methodological variations that might influence interoceptive outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical framing using interoceptive predictive coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a predictive coding model of interoception and dissociation as a theoretical account linking interoceptive deficits to dissociative experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation and synthesis may be organized around predictive coding ideas (mismatches in expectancies and predictions about the environment leading to disconnection/derealization); use theory to contextualize empirical patterns but distinguish empirical findings from theoretical interpretation.
